title.purpose: Page titles only; one per screen, flush over a seam. Face swaps per palette along with --font-ui.

body.purpose: All UI text, form labels, table cells, prose.

label.purpose: Panel nameplates, table column heads, section markers. The single small-caps treatment.

data.purpose: Figures, timestamps, IDs, paths. Opt-in via data-mono; never for prose. Face swaps per palette (Spline Sans Mono / Azeret Mono / Chivo Mono).

motion.name: ease-console
motion.purpose: The world's single easing curve; all state transitions and the one authored moment.

motion.name: panel-in
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: a panel expanding along one axis (scale 1 0.94 -> 1 1, opacity 0 -> 1).

lightTheme.note: Same rack, daylight. Identical seams and restraint; the graphite ladder inverts to a cool engineering surface and the state inks darken so white text clears AA. Defined under .light in packages/ui/src/globals.css.

themes.label: Graphite
themes.hint: Dark instrument console, cool blue accent.
themes.note: Canonical palette. Also the :root / .light fallback, so an unknown or absent data-theme degrades to Graphite.

themes.label: Ledger
themes.hint: Cool paper, ink rules, soft corners.
themes.note: Light is its natural state; dark is the same ledger under a dim lamp.

themes.label: Ember
themes.hint: Warm near-black steel, ember accent, Chivo.
themes.note: Tightest state separation in the system: accent sits 40 degrees from warning and 40 from destructive.

themeContract.selector: html carries a mode class (.dark / .light) and data-theme="<id>" as two independent attributes; themed blocks are [data-theme="x"].dark | .light at (0,2,0), beating a bare mode class at (0,1,0).
themeContract.preHydration: apps/dashboard/index.html applies both before first paint. The palette id is applied verbatim with no whitelist — an unknown id falls through to Graphite, so adding a palette never requires editing that file.
themeContract.selfContained: Every palette+mode block re-specifies every other token, including --font-ui / --font-data, so a nested data-theme element resolves its own palette AND fonts.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled accent control per view region. Hard-edged panel action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2.25rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: calc(var(--radius) * 0.8); background: var(--primary); color: var(--primary-foreground); font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 100ms var(--ease-console), border-color 100ms var(--ease-console), color 100ms var(--ease-console); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary) 85%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 40%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary structural action. Carries the opaque control boundary.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2.25rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) * 0.8); background: transparent; color: var(--foreground); font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 100ms var(--ease-console), border-color 100ms var(--ease-console); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--muted); border-color: var(--border); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 40%, transparent); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Quiet at rest by doctrine; gains weight only on focus. Must be isolated from its neighbours.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2.25rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 40%, transparent); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) * 0.8); background: transparent; color: var(--destructive); font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 100ms var(--ease-console); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 10%, transparent); } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--destructive); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 30%, transparent); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Inset field with an opaque, discoverable boundary distinct from decorative seams.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 2.25rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border: 1px solid var(--input); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) * 0.8); background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted) 40%, transparent); color: var(--foreground); font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.875rem; outline: none; transition: border-color 100ms var(--ease-console), box-shadow 100ms var(--ease-console); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--ring); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring) 40%, transparent); } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--destructive); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 25%, transparent); }

components.name: Panel with Header
components.description: The world's structural unit. No border on the panel itself; the seam belongs to the grid container.
components.css: .ds-panel { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 0; background: var(--card); color: var(--card-foreground); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) * 0.8); overflow: hidden; } .ds-panel-header { display: flex; height: 2.25rem; flex-shrink: 0; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.75rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); padding: 0 0.75rem; } .ds-panel-label { margin: 0; font-size: var(--text-label-size); font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: var(--tracking-label); text-transform: uppercase; line-height: 1.2; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-panel-aside { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground); } .ds-panel-body { display: flex; flex: 1 1 auto; flex-direction: column; min-width: 0; padding: 0.75rem; } .ds-panel-grid { display: grid; gap: 1px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: calc(var(--radius) * 0.8); background: var(--border); overflow: hidden; }

components.name: Theme Picker
components.description: Settings-only palette surface: a mode toggle plus a visible list of palettes, each row showing a swatch, label, and hint, with the selected row checked. The avatar dropdown no longer carries the palette list — it exposes only ThemeModeToggle, the ghost button that flips light/dark. The real swatch re-themes itself by carrying data-theme plus the current mode class, which is why every palette block in globals.css is self-contained; the snippet approximates that layering with host tokens, because a self-contained snippet cannot load those blocks.

narrative.overview:
An internal tool is equipment, not a brochure. The interface is built as a rack of bays: flat graphite modules bolted to a shared seam grid, each with a small-caps nameplate, each showing measured values. Nothing floats, nothing glows, nothing is decorated. What a border does here is structural — a 1px seam is the edge of a bay, and a lighter graphite step is one more unit of elevation.

The system is dark-first because that is the working condition it was chosen for: a console that sits open all day beside an editor, read for state at a glance rather than savoured. Its light mode is the same rack under daylight — a cool engineering surface, never cream — with the same seams and the same restraint.

The rack ships in three palettes. Graphite is the canonical one described throughout this document. Ledger re-clothes it as cool paper with ink rules and soft corners; Ember warms it to near-black steel with an ember accent. What changes between them is palette, typeface, and corner radius — and nothing else. The seams, the elevation order, the state vocabulary, and the mono-for-data rule are the world's constants. See Themes.

Colour is the system's most disciplined decision. Saturation is reserved exclusively for state, and it is drawn from the colours a developer already reads fluently in syntax: keyword blue, string green, value amber, error red, comment violet. A user learns the vocabulary once, in code, and it carries into the interface. The primary accent appears on a single control per view; everything else earns its colour by meaning something.
keyCharacteristics: Depth from 1px hairline seams and three measured ground steps — never from shadow
Saturation spent only on state, using syntax-derived semantics
Hard, instrument-panel geometry; corner radius is a per-palette decision (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.375rem)
Monospace reserved for figures, IDs, and measurement — never as a technical costume
Panel headers as tracked small caps; body in a compact grotesk
Three palettes — Graphite, Ledger, Ember — each shipping light and dark; only palette, typeface, and radius vary

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Saturation exists to mean something. A colour that does not encode state does not appear. If a screen needs emphasis and has no state to report, the answer is weight, scale, or a seam — not hue.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: The primary accent fills at most one control per view region. Its scarcity is what makes the primary action unambiguous.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace is applied to figures, identifiers, timestamps, and measured values — and to nothing else. Prose in a monospace face is a costume, and this system does not wear it. In the table primitive this is enforced structurally: cells are sans by default and opt in with data-mono.

rules.name: The One Label Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one small-caps label treatment. It lives in .panel-label and consumes --text-label-size / --tracking-label; primitives consume the same tokens. Two label treatments is a bug.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: If an element looks like it needs a shadow to separate from its background, the ground step is wrong. Fix the step, not the shadow. Zero-offset halos and offset drop shadows are both decoration here.

rules.name: The One Step Rule
rules.body: A surface takes one step of elevation, never two. Nested elevation is how card-inside-card layouts happen; panels contain seams and content, not lifted panels.

rules.name: The Self-Contained Palette Rule
rules.body: Every palette+mode block re-specifies every themeable token. A block that silently inherits a colour from another palette is a bug: it breaks nested previews and any future data-theme scoping. --ease-console, --text-label-size, and --tracking-label are deliberately global and inherited.

rules.name: The Two-Axis Rule
rules.body: Mode and palette are independent. No palette is "the dark one" or "the light one" — every palette ships both, so a new palette defines two blocks, never one.

dos: Do separate surfaces with a 1px seam and the next graphite step; build seams into the grid container with gap-px, not onto each panel.
Do spend colour only on state, drawing from the syntax vocabulary (blue keyword, green string, amber value, red error, violet comment).
Do use .panel-label for every nameplate and column head; it is the one small-caps treatment.
Do opt figures, IDs, and timestamps into mono with data-mono, and add tabular-nums where columns must align.
Do keep the control boundary (--input) opaque and distinct from the decorative seam (--border) — one must be found, the other must not compete.
Do isolate destructive actions and leave them quiet until focused.

Do resolve every colour, radius, and font through the token blocks in packages/ui/src/globals.css; a clone must be able to re-skin the world by editing that one file. The header carries only ThemeModeToggle — palette selection lives on Settings.

Do add a palette by writing exactly two token blocks ([data-theme="x"].dark and .light) plus one entry in packages/ui/src/themes.ts — nothing else. A new exports subpath needs a dev-server restart before the app can resolve it.
donts: Don't add a shadow, gradient, or decorative blur. There is no shadow vocabulary; fix the ground step instead.
Don't invent a radius outside the palette's --radius scale, and don't round a container into a pill — the cap is --radius x 1.4 by construction.
Don't let a palette change the seam grammar, the elevation order, the state vocabulary, or the mono-for-data rule. A palette varies colour, typeface, and radius only.
Don't use monospace for prose, labels, or decorative "technical" flavour.
Don't tint a large surface with a state colour; state lives in dots, borders, and text, not in panels.
Don't nest lifted surfaces — one step of elevation per surface, and no card inside a card.
Don't add a second small-caps label treatment or a second state-chip implementation; extend the existing one.
Don't reintroduce a same-size card grid as a page structure — panels are asymmetric and priority-ordered.
